quality_tests.label: As first run
quality_tests.how: Average 12-month return against the average of every stock, early-stage included

quality_tests.label: Against the middle stock
quality_tests.how: Median return against the median stock, so a few huge winners count once each

quality_tests.label: Within each sector
quality_tests.how: Share of same-sector stocks each one beat over the year (50% is average), so an oil boom or an AI-power boom cancels out

quality_tests.label: Within each sector, no early-stage
quality_tests.how: Same, with early-stage companies left out, since the formula is not built for them

quality_tests.label: Over three years
quality_tests.how: Three-year return against the middle stock, early-stage left out; fewer dates qualify

price_tests.label: Within each sector
price_tests.how: Share of same-sector stocks each one beat over the year

price_tests.label: Over three years
price_tests.how: Three-year return against the middle stock

tests.name: Strong beats Weak
tests.detail: Strong stocks averaged +0.1 points against the group each year; Weak and Broken averaged +7.5.

tests.name: Buying in the zone beats buying rich
tests.detail: Stocks at Deep discount or in the Buy zone averaged -11.5 points against the group; Full or Stretched averaged -3.6.

notes: Price return only; dividends are not included, which understates returns for utilities, pipelines and oil producers.
Policy and Outside pressure are excluded because they come from a hand-kept log that cannot be honestly back-dated.
The stock list was chosen in 2026, so companies that failed or were bought out earlier are missing. This survivorship bias flatters every band equally but should be kept in mind.
Excess return is each stock's 12-month return minus the average of all stocks scored on the same date.
